summary: CCC-era 100-ft MC-39 fire tower in Monroe County, Alabama, administered by the AFC; last staffed until 1982, found locked in 1983; current condition unknown.

facts.design: 100-foot MC-39 tower with 7 by 7 foot cab

events.note: Register description and blog give 1939 at CCC camp P-76; the register's Built field reads 1941
Gary Cole, a forest ranger assigned to north Monroe County, began in June 1976
Cole manned the tower until 1982, when he became county forestry supervisor
Blog author last got to climb the tower; it was locked that day and the author did not enter the cab

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's description and the blog say 1939 at CCC camp P-76; the register's Built field says 1941. Recorded as 1939 with the 1941 figure noted. Sources disagree; the build year is not settled.
The register gives US 850, AL 28; the blog gives US 850, AL 29. The register number is used in facts.

notes_for_editor: Staffing, the 1983 locked visit and the Findley family come from one personal blog written by a former visitor whose grandfather worked as a tower man here; treat them as recollection. The 1819 News column is by Thomas Kaufmann, who also nominated this tower to the register; it is used only for statewide context. No source found gives current condition or public access, so facts omit access and status: the register has no condition field, and the earlier 'standing' status was not supported by the register text. The 1939 vs 1941 build year is unresolved. Search snippets described a 12-by-12 foot wooden cab for this tower; that is not in the fetched blog text and is not used. OSM node 358979936 shows a tower at about 132 m elevation but gives no history; not cited. No photos added.
